sources.entry: faiss-cpu - A library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors.

summary.one_liner: Faiss is a C++ library with Python/numpy wrappers for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors, with optional GPU acceleration.
summary.what_it_does: Faiss stores sets of vectors in index types and searches them by L2 distance or dot product, with cosine similarity supported via normalized vectors. It offers exact baseline search as well as compressed-domain methods (binary vectors and quantization codes) that can scale to billions of vectors in main memory on one server. Graph-based structures such as HNSW and NSG add an indexing layer over raw vectors for faster search. It also includes k-means clustering and supporting code for evaluation and parameter tuning. GPU versions of indexes (e.g., GpuIndexFlatL2 in place of IndexFlatL2) accept CPU or GPU input, and single and multi-GPU usage is supported. The README says it is developed primarily at Meta's Fundamental AI Research group.
how_to_run: conda install -c pytorch faiss-cpu (precompiled Anaconda packages: faiss-cpu, faiss-gpu, faiss-gpu-cuvs)
Build from source with cmake; see INSTALL.md for details
Requires a BLAS implementation; GPU support optionally via CUDA or AMD ROCm
notable: Indexes span exact search, compressed binary and quantization codes, and graph methods like HNSW and NSG
GPU indexes can be drop-in replacements for CPU indexes
Research citations provided for the Faiss library and billion-scale GPU search
caveats: GPU features require CUDA or ROCm and a GPU-equipped server
Building from source requires cmake and a BLAS dependency; details are in INSTALL.md
Compressed methods trade search precision for memory savings
